_comment: First real static timing analysis of railnet_top in sky130. PRE-LAYOUT: ideal clocks, no placement, no routing, no extracted parasitics. This is not Gate 6 sign-off; post-route numbers will be worse. Committed because results/ and build/ are gitignored.
status: PARTIAL - post-synthesis STA done, sign-off STA still open

derived.how: 20.0 ns period - 8.70 ns setup slack = 11.30 ns critical path; 1/11.30 ns = 88.5 MHz

reading: railnet_top closes 50 MHz comfortably in sky130 at the gate level, but the implied ceiling is about 88 MHz - well under half the 200 MHz the repository has carried as an architectural target. That target remains unproven and now has a pre-layout figure arguing against it.
caveats: Post-synthesis STA: ideal clock, no clock tree, no placement, no routing, no SPEF parasitics
Post-route numbers are normally worse, so 88 MHz is an optimistic ceiling, not a result
Memories are flip-flops here (no SRAM macro is wired in), so this netlist is the 317,850-cell variant, not the 39,706-cell logic-only one
Single corner only (the flow's default), not multi-corner sign-off
next_step: Let the flow finish placement, CTS and routing, then read the post-route sign-off STA. After that, re-run at CLOCK_PERIOD 5.0 to test the 200 MHz claim directly.
